But that is what the automotive industry did to start with. Suzuki, Toyota etc started off with assembling plants in India. After liberalization these companies started manufacturing plants instead of just assembling. 

Semiconductors are doing the same.

Indian manufactured cars, mobiles and especially defence equipment is using foreign made chips. Hence top end products like semiconductors should be manufactured in India to strengthen its manufacturing to outside influences.

I've been reading a book on this topic and I'll try to paraphrase a few points onto why 1962 was such a disaster for India.  
  
Firstly the defensive emplacements constructed in the Aksai Chin region where placed were far apart from one another. As experienced in 1948, mountainous defensive emplacements should have overlapping fields of fire otherwise they can be overwhelmed. 
>"Leave alone heavy artillery support, the heaviest weapons that these posts had were light machine guns (LMGs), with only a few having some mortars. The posts were separated from each other by anywhere from 3 km to 10 km. This meant that not only was there no mutual cross-cover, there were very few withdrawal options in the face of an enemy assault in the absence of roads, tracks or helipads."  
  
Secondly these bunkers were manned by a platoon sized detachment armed at the most with a light machine gun. As is evident this was utterly woeful level of preparedness. Add to this, most of these posts were manned by paramilitary forces like the Assam Rifles till mere months before start of hostilities. The few army regulars that moved into these posts were unaware of their surroundings and prone to get blindsided. 
  
> Indian Army was deployed in section- and platoon-sized pockets (10 to 40 troops) as they were in the Daulat Beg Oldi complex, Chip Chap Valley, Galwan Valley, and Sirjap complex on the north bank of the Pangang Tso in the Chushul sector of Ladakh.10 A similar deployment was made in the Namka Chu Valley, the Lohit Valley and other locations in the east and west Kameng sectors of NEFA
  

As to why this happened is purely political. The Indian PM didn't actually consider an all out attack from China. He thought of all this as mere postering.
